claims.text: The modeled FeNiCrCoCu coating is 21 Å thick and is adhered to a 100 Å × 100 Å × 55 Å single-crystal Cu substrate with FCC [100], [010], and [001] orientations.
The test uses a virtual indenter moving at 10 m/s to a depth of 30 Å, with loading and unloading intervals of 300 ps.
The coating is evaluated at 300 K, 600 K, 900 K, and 1200 K, using 300 K as the baseline.
At 300–600 K, the coating lattice remains ordered.
Dislocation density remains stable from 300 K to 600 K.
Above approximately 900 K, rapid lattice disorder develops in the coating.
Above approximately 900 K, dislocation density decreases significantly.
Above approximately 900 K, the fraction of atoms classified as HCP increases.
The high-temperature structural changes shift deformation from stacking-fault-mediated plasticity to lattice-disorder-controlled plasticity.
Around 600 K, a slight reduction in dislocation density causes a modest increase in elastic modulus.
Hardness remains relatively stable between 300 K and 600 K.
Overall wear resistance remains relatively stable between 300 K and 600 K.
Above approximately 900 K, hardness decreases sharply because of lattice disorder and softening.
Above approximately 900 K, elastic modulus decreases sharply because of lattice disorder and softening.
Above approximately 900 K, overall wear resistance decreases sharply.
Above approximately 900 K, tangential force increases and exhibits stronger fluctuations.
Above approximately 900 K, the friction coefficient increases and exhibits stronger fluctuations.
The room-temperature coating has an ordered lattice and a higher dislocation density that ensure stable wear resistance and hardness.
Changes in wear properties should correlate with increased lattice disorder, increased HCP fraction, and decreased dislocation density.

contradictions.description: The structural-mediator field says dislocation density is stable throughout 300–600 K, whereas the mechanism field says it is already slightly reduced around 600 K.
